prompt: A session row's VoiceOver label is `SQL Databases, 50 minutes, Monday 19 October`. Where does `done` belong?
hint: It is the part that changes.

choices.text: At the end of the label, after the day
choices.why: The label is what the row is; putting state in it makes every row longer to scan.

choices.text: In the value
choices.why: Right: the value is the state, and VoiceOver announces it when it changes.

choices.text: In the hint, read after a pause
choices.why: A hint says what an action does, and people turn hints off.

choices.text: Nowhere: the tick shows it
choices.why: The tick is invisible to a person who cannot see it.

prompt: Why does `spokenLabel` say `minutes` where the screen shows `min`?
hint: Think of how a voice reads an abbreviation.

choices.text: Because `min` is not valid inside a Swift string
choices.why: Any text is valid in a string; this is about the ear.

choices.text: To make the label longer than the value
choices.why: Length is not the aim; being understood is.

choices.text: A voice reads `min` as letters or as another word
choices.why: Right: an abbreviation obvious to the eye is ambiguous to the ear.

choices.text: VoiceOver refuses labels with abbreviations in them
choices.why: It reads whatever it is given, which is the problem.

prompt: Why is the day formatted with `setLocalizedDateFormatFromTemplate` rather than built by joining a weekday, a number and a month?

choices.text: Joining strings is slower than a formatter
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; the test is about language.

choices.text: Each language orders a date its own way, with its own words between
choices.why: Right: Portuguese reads `segunda-feira, 19 de outubro`, with a `de` nobody would join in.

choices.text: Linux has no names for the days of the week
choices.why: It does: the test printed them on Linux.

choices.text: A template stops VoiceOver reading the digits
choices.why: Any day name avoids reading digits; the template is about each language's order.

prompt: The text VoiceOver reads after a pause, saying what acting on the element will do, and which experienced users turn off, is its ___.
hint: Neither the label nor the value.

prompt: How many tests passed in `~/l19`, counting lesson 1's?
hint: The last line of the run.

prompt: A `Text` with `onTapGesture` marks a session done. What does a VoiceOver user miss?

choices.text: Nothing, since the tap works with a double-tap
choices.why: They are not told it can be activated, so they have no reason to try.

choices.text: That it is a control at all
choices.why: Right: it is read as text. A `Button` carries `.isButton` and says so.

choices.text: Only the colour that shows it is done
choices.why: The colour is a separate problem; the missing trait is the main one here.

choices.text: The label, which `onTapGesture` removes from the element
choices.why: The label stays; the trait is what is missing.

prompt: `Text(title).font(.headline)` looks like a heading. What makes it one for VoiceOver?
hint: The font is for the eye.

choices.text: Nothing more: `.headline` sets the heading trait
choices.why: The font says nothing to VoiceOver.

choices.text: Wrapping it in a `Section`
choices.why: A section header helps in a `List`, but the general answer is the trait.

choices.text: `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)`
choices.why: Right, and then the rotor can jump to it.

choices.text: A bold font weight of at least semibold
choices.why: Weight is visual; it is the trait that is heard.

prompt: How does a VoiceOver user reach a list row's `swipeActions`?

choices.text: As custom actions, by swiping up or down
choices.why: Right: SwiftUI offers them to VoiceOver on its own.

choices.text: They cannot; swipe actions are for sighted users
choices.why: SwiftUI exposes them as custom actions.

choices.text: By a three-finger swipe left on the row
choices.why: Three fingers scroll; the actions are on the rotor.

choices.text: Through a hint the app must write for each
choices.why: A hint describes; it does not perform.

prompt: The course row has a title, the week's minutes and an *Add session* button. Which child behaviour fits it?
hint: The button must stay its own stop.

choices.text: `.ignore`, with a label for the whole row
choices.why: `.ignore` silences the children, the button included.

choices.text: `.combine`
choices.why: One element would merge the button into the text.

choices.text: `.contain`
choices.why: Right: the children stay separate, grouped as a container.

choices.text: Hide the button, and add a custom action on the row instead
choices.why: Possible, but it hides a visible control; the section's choice is `.contain`.

prompt: What is the default `children:` behaviour of `accessibilityElement`?

choices.text: `.combine`
choices.why: Combine has to be asked for.

choices.text: `.ignore`
choices.why: Right: one element, children silent.

choices.text: `.contain`
choices.why: Contain has to be asked for.

choices.text: There is none; the argument is required
choices.why: It has a default, `.ignore`.

prompt: A colleague hides the session row's tick with `.accessibilityHidden(true)` because it is "just an icon". What is lost?

choices.text: Nothing, as decorative images should be hidden
choices.why: The tick is information, not decoration.

choices.text: The button trait, which the tick provided
choices.why: The tick was never a button.

choices.text: Whether the session is done, unless the value says it
choices.why: Right: section 02's row moves it into the value, which is why hiding the icon is then safe.

choices.text: The row's position in the reading order
choices.why: Order follows the layout, not the icon.

prompt: Match each behaviour to what VoiceOver hears for the session row.

pairs.right: One stop: the sentence the app wrote
One stop: the children's labels joined

prompt: Which font follows the person's text size setting?

choices.text: `.font(.system(size: 17))`
choices.why: A point size is fixed whatever the setting.

choices.text: `.font(.body)`
choices.why: Right: a text style follows Dynamic Type.

choices.text: `.font(.system(size: 17, weight: .regular))`
choices.why: Adding a weight does not make a point size scale.

choices.text: `.font(.custom("Plex", fixedSize: 17))`
choices.why: `fixedSize` says it in its name.

prompt: At an accessibility text size the course title and the minutes no longer fit on one line. What does the section recommend?
hint: Change the layout, never the size.

choices.text: Cap the row with `.dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.large)`
choices.why: That undoes the person's choice.

choices.text: Shrink the text with `.minimumScaleFactor(0.5)`
choices.why: Shrinking returns the text to the size the person said they cannot read.

choices.text: Stack it vertically, or let `ViewThatFits` choose
choices.why: Right: the layout adapts and the size stays the person's.

choices.text: Hide the minutes at accessibility sizes
choices.why: That removes information from the people who asked for larger text.

prompt: What is `@ScaledMetric` for?

choices.text: Sizes that should grow with the text, like an icon's
choices.why: Right: twenty points at the default grows in step with `.body`.

choices.text: Measuring the contrast of a colour
choices.why: Contrast is section 07's formula, not a property wrapper.

choices.text: Fixing a value so it never changes with the setting
choices.why: It does the opposite.

choices.text: Converting points to pixels on each screen
choices.why: Points to pixels is the screen's scale, not Dynamic Type.

prompt: Put the steps of a first VoiceOver test in order.
items: Triple-click the side button to turn VoiceOver on
Swipe right through each element of the screen
Write down every place you had to look
Triple-click again to turn it off

prompt: What does the Accessibility Inspector's audit catch, and what does it not?

choices.text: Everything VoiceOver would say wrong
choices.why: It cannot judge whether a label makes sense.

choices.text: Missing labels and low contrast, but not whether a label makes sense
choices.why: Right: listening answers the rest.

choices.text: Only crashes in the simulator
choices.why: Crashes are the debugger's; the audit is about accessibility.

choices.text: Nothing until the app is on the App Store
choices.why: It runs against the simulator in Xcode.

prompt: What contrast ratio does WCAG 2.2 AA ask for ordinary text? Give the first number of the ratio.
`contrast.swift` gave the darker green tick 4.40:1 on white. What may it be used for?

choices.text: Any text, since it rounds to 4.5
choices.why: The threshold is a minimum, not a rounding.

choices.text: Nothing: it fails like the brighter green
choices.why: It passes the 3:1 bar for icons and large text.

choices.text: The tick, and large text
choices.why: Right, which is why the word beside it uses the grey that passed.

choices.text: Only the dark theme
choices.why: It was measured on white; the dark theme is measured separately.

prompt: Why does the ratio add 0.05 to both luminances?
hint: Without it, black on white would divide by zero.

choices.text: To round the result to two decimals
choices.why: The rounding is in the `String(format:)`.

choices.text: It stands for the light a screen reflects
choices.why: Right, and it is why black on white is 21 rather than infinite.

choices.text: To make green count more than red and blue
choices.why: That is the weights, 0.7152 for green.

choices.text: To undo the sRGB curve
choices.why: That is the `pow` in `luminance`.

prompt: Which of these would a VoiceOver user notice in the planner? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think of what is heard, not what is seen.

choices.text: A heading without `.isHeader`
choices.why: Yes: the rotor cannot find it.

choices.text: A placeholder in light grey
choices.why: That is a contrast problem, for people who can see a little.

choices.text: A row read as four fragments
choices.why: Yes: too many stops, and no sentence.

choices.text: An icon 20 points wide at the default size
choices.why: Size is for the eye; VoiceOver reads the label.

prompt: Which part of this lesson ran on Linux?

choices.text: The `SessionRow` view with its modifiers
choices.why: SwiftUI does not exist on Linux.

choices.text: The Accessibility Inspector's audit
choices.why: It ships with Xcode, on a Mac.

choices.text: The spoken labels and the contrast ratios
choices.why: Right: both are functions of plain values.

choices.text: A VoiceOver session with the screen covered
choices.why: That needs a simulator or a phone.
